title: Saffron Chicken with French Lentils
ingredients: 7 whole chicken legs, split into thighs and drumsticks (14 pieces, roughly 5 lb)
1 1/2 cups (300 g) French lentils (lentilles du Puy), rinsed
3 1/2 cups chicken stock + 1 cup white wine (4 1/2 cups liquid total)
Parsley leaves, finely chopped, to finish
steps: BROWN THE CHICKEN: Heat the oven to 350°F. Season the chicken generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high and sear the chicken on all sides until well browned, in batches if needed. Remove and set aside.

MIREPOIX: Lower to medium. Add the shallots, carrot, celery and parsley stalks if using, with a pinch of salt. Cook 5-6 min until softened. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, then stir in the paprika and cumin and cook briefly to bloom.

LENTILS AND STOCK: Add the lentils and stir to coat in the aromatics. In a small saucepan, warm the stock and wine with the saffron and a few pinches of salt - taste and adjust seasoning before it goes in.

Pour the saffron liquid into the pan and add the bay leaves. Nestle the chicken back on top of the lentils in a single layer. Squeeze one lemon half over everything and add a few more cracks of pepper.
Transfer to the oven and bake uncovered 45-55 min, until the lentils are tender and the chicken is fully cooked.
FINISH: Rest 5 min out of the oven. Pull the bay leaves. Squeeze the remaining lemon half over the top and finish with chopped parsley.
notes: SIZE: 7 whole legs is about 5 lb of bone-in chicken - that is a party or a big-batch cook, not a weeknight. One whole leg (thigh + drumstick) per person feeds 7 generously; with the lentils filling it out, 6-8 depending on appetite. TO HALVE: 3-4 legs, 3/4 cup lentils, 1 3/4 cups stock + 1/2 cup wine, same pan and times. LIQUID: the original lists 4 1/2 cups stock with wine subbed in for 1 cup - that reads as 3 1/2 cups stock + 1 cup wine. Needs a pan wide enough to hold the chicken in ONE layer or the skin steams instead of crisping. Bloom the paprika in the fat, don't skip it - that is where the color and depth come from. Warming the saffron in the stock first is what actually extracts it.

title: Japanese Curry Chicken Potpie
ingredients: 1 1/4 cups chopped unpeeled Yukon gold potatoes (1/2-inch)
1 (3.2-oz) package mild Japanese curry mix, cubed (Golden Curry)
1/2 (17.3-oz) package frozen puff pastry, thawed - 1 sheet (Pepperidge Farm)
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Heat the oil in a 10-inch cast iron skillet over medium until shimmering. Add onion, carrots and potatoes and cook, stirring frequently, until the carrots and potatoes just start to soften, 4-5 min.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 min.
Add the stock and bring to a boil over medium-high, stirring occasionally. Reduce to medium-low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are fork tender, 8-10 min.
Stir in the curry mix, ketchup and salt until dissolved and the mixture thickens, about 2 min. Stir in the chicken until evenly distributed. Remove from heat and keep warm.

Roll the pastry on a lightly floured surface into a 13-inch square. Lay it over the skillet and trim, leaving a 3/4- to 1-inch overhang. Fold the pastry under itself so the rolled edge is flush with the top of the skillet, then crimp into the side with a fork. It's fine if it doesn't adhere perfectly.
Brush the top with beaten egg and cut 8 slits (1 1/2-2 inches) to vent.
Bake until the pastry is golden brown and the filling is bubbly, about 30 min. Let stand 15 min before serving - this is not optional, it needs to set.
notes: Uses a store-bought Japanese curry roux block (Golden Curry, mild) from the international aisle - that's what makes the sauce silky and gravy-thick. Ketchup is the sweetness that makes it read as Japanese curry rather than generic. Rotisserie chicken keeps it a weeknight dish; skip the chicken for a vegetarian version. MAKE AHEAD: filling keeps 3 days in the fridge; loosen with a Tbsp or two of water and reheat gently over medium-low before topping. Bake the pastry fresh - it doesn't survive reheating crisp.

title: Spaghetti with Lemon Pesto
ingredients: 4 lemons (for zest only - about 2/3 cup wide zest strips)
Kosher salt and ground black pepper
1 oz Parmesan, no rind, in rough 1-inch pieces, plus finely grated for serving
1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for serving
steps: With a vegetable peeler, take the zest off the lemons in long wide strips - colored peel only, none of the white pith. You want about 2/3 cup.
Combine 2 quarts water, 1 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar and HALF the zest strips in a large pot. Bring to a boil and cook 2 min, then fish out and discard that zest.
Add the spaghetti to the same water and cook until al dente. Reserve 1 1/2 cups cooking water, then drain and return the pasta to the pot.

In a food processor, combine the remaining zest, almonds, Parmesan, remaining 1/2 tsp sugar, and 1/4 tsp each salt and pepper. Process to the texture of coarse sand, 10-20 sec. Add the oil and process 10 sec more.
Add the pesto and 3/4 cup of the reserved pasta water to the spaghetti and toss. Add more water as needed until the sauce coats the strands.
Toss in the chives, season with salt and pepper, and serve drizzled with more oil and grated Parmesan.
notes: The lemons are used for zest only - no juice - so save the naked lemons for something else. Boiling half the zest in the pasta water is the trick: it perfumes the pasta itself before the raw zest goes into the pesto. Peel with a vegetable peeler, not a microplane; the pith is what turns it bitter. Reserve more pasta water than you think you need.

ingredients: 4.5 oz ginger juice (roughly 8-10 oz fresh ginger)
90 chopped cilantro stems - stems, not leaves (1 large bunch)
Kosher or sea salt, about 1.5 tsp to start
PER DRINK, if you ever do scale down: 1/2 oz lime, 1/2 oz orange, 1/4 oz ginger juice, 3 jalapeno slices, 5 cilantro stems, 1 onion slice
components.name: Leche de Tigre base
steps: Combine the juices, jalapeno, cilantro stems and red onion in a large nonreactive container.
Macerate at room temperature for 1 hour. Don't shortcut this - the hour is where the spice and umami come from.
Fine-strain, pressing gently on the solids. Press, don't wring: hard pressing pulls bitterness out of the onion.
Salt the strained liquid and stir to dissolve. Start with 1.5 tsp, taste, add more - it should be bright, savory and clearly salted.
Yield should be about 19-20 oz, enough for 15 drinks at 1 1/4 oz each. Keeps refrigerated about 2 days; batch it for the night you're pouring.
components.why: This is the whole drink - the spirits are just the vehicle. All the acid, heat and savory depth comes from the base, and it needs a full hour of maceration, so it gets made first and it gets made in bulk. Amounts below are scaled for 15 drinks with a 20% buffer built in, because straining leaves liquid behind in the solids. Taste it before you build anything: the salt is what makes it read as ceviche rather than a sour.

ingredients: 18 3/4 oz Leche de Tigre base (make this first - see above)
45 jalapeno slices, for garnish (3 per drink)
PER DRINK: 1 1/4 oz base, 1/2 oz simple syrup, 3/4 oz mezcal, 3/4 oz tequila
notes: Scaled for 15. Shopping: one 750ml bottle each of mezcal and tequila covers it with about 14 oz left over; 1 cup sugar + 1 cup water makes ~12 oz simple syrup, more than the 7.5 oz you need. Total liquid before ice is about 48 oz, roughly 1.5 quarts. Produce counts are approximate - juice yields vary, so buy a couple extra limes. Split mezcal/tequila keeps the smoke mild; go heavier on mezcal if you want it smokier. Base goes flat after ~2 days, so make it the day of or the day before.
steps: Build to order: add 1 1/4 oz base, 1/2 oz simple syrup, 3/4 oz mezcal and 3/4 oz tequila to a shaker with ice. Shake until fully combined and well chilled.
Fine-strain into a chilled rocks glass over fresh ice. Garnish with 3 jalapeno slices.

To batch ahead: combine the base, simple syrup, mezcal and tequila in a pitcher (about 48 oz total) and refrigerate. Shake 3 1/4 oz per drink with ice to order - don't pre-dilute the whole pitcher, it goes flat and watery.
title: Leche de Tigre
totalTime: 1 hr 5 min (1 hr of it hands-off)

ingredients: Sea salt and black pepper, for seasoning the chicken
1 tsp chicken Better Than Bouillon, or 1 bouillon cube
To serve: tostada shells or corn tortillas, Mexican rice, refried beans, shredded green cabbage, sliced radishes, cotija or queso fresco, avocado
notes: 2 chipotles is my baseline - add more if you want it hotter. Enchilada sauce replaces the taco seasoning; if you don't have it, use 2-3 oz taco seasoning instead. Chicken thighs replace the 4 cups of cooked shredded chicken - you can still use 4 cups shredded if you want the fast 30-min version, in which case skip the browning and the oven braise entirely. Leftovers keep 5 days in the fridge, 3 months frozen.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Season the chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a deep oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high and brown the thighs on both sides. Remove the chicken to a plate, leaving the browned bits and juices in the pot.
Add the onion to the same pot and cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 6 min. Reduce to medium, add the garlic, and cook until fragrant, about 1 min.

Add the chipotles, adobo sauce, oregano, enchilada sauce, fire roasted tomatoes and bouillon. Return the chicken and any juices to the pot. Bring to a simmer over medium and cook at least 10 min, stirring occasionally.

Cover the pot and move it to the oven. Braise at 350°F for 3-4 hours. At about the 3-hour mark, check the chicken - if it's ready, shred it right in the pot, then return it to the oven at 325°F for another 30-60 min. It's servable any time after that first check.
Taste and adjust salt and adobo. Serve warm on tostadas or tortillas, or over rice, with cabbage, radishes, cotija and avocado.
title: Chicken Tinga (Jarred's braised version)

ingredients: 1 tsp sea salt, plus more to taste
1 (15.5-oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15.5-oz) can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 (15.5-oz) can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
To serve: cilantro, green onions, sour cream, grated cheddar, sliced avocado
notes: The 1/2 cup chili powder sounds like a lot - it's mild, adding smokiness rather than heat. Heat comes from the optional cayenne and Tapatio. Keeps 3-4 days in the fridge, up to 3 months frozen. Long simmer is doing the real work here.
steps: Heat a large Dutch oven or pot over medium-high. Add beef, pork, onion, both peppers, garlic, salt and pepper. Cook, breaking up the meat with a wooden spoon, until browned, 8-10 min.
Add beans, tomatoes, enchilada sauce, chili powder, cumin, bay leaves, sugar, and the cayenne and hot sauce if using. Pour in enough water to cover the beans (about 1-2 cups) and stir well.
Bring to a boil over high, then reduce to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, at least 1-2 hours - up to 8 hours for best flavor.
Taste and adjust salt. Ladle into bowls and top with cilantro, green onions, sour cream, cheese and avocado.
SLOW COOKER: brown the meat mixture in a skillet as in step 1, transfer to the slow cooker, add everything from step 2, stir, and cook on high 4 hours or low 8 hours.
title: Award Winning Chili

ingredients: 1/2 tsp thinly sliced red Thai chile, plus more to garnish
3 cups reduced-sodium chicken or vegetable broth
32 frozen mini wontons (pork, chicken or vegetable)
Garnish: cilantro, Thai basil, scallions, sliced red chile, crushed peanuts, lime wedges
notes: Swap spinach or napa cabbage for the bok choy; any frozen dumpling works. Chili oil drizzle for extra heat. Leftovers keep 2 days max - dumplings go mushy after that.
steps: Heat oil in a large saucepan or medium Dutch oven over medium-high. Brown the mushrooms, stirring occasionally, 5-8 min.
Drop to medium. Add shallot, garlic, ginger, chile and salt; stir often until the shallots soften, 1-2 min.
Stir in the curry paste and cook, stirring constantly, until slightly darkened and very fragrant, about 1 min.
Add broth, coconut milk, fish sauce, lime juice and brown sugar. Bring to a simmer over medium-high.

Add the wontons, return to a simmer, then stir in the bok choy. Reduce to medium and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the dumplings are cooked through and the bok choy is tender-crisp, 3-5 min.
Divide among bowls, garnish, and serve immediately.
title: Red Curry Dumpling Soup
